title: Who is on the lowest floor?
description: Four friends stand in four shops of the tall block. Each shop's floor is read from the picture, the floors are put on one line, and the one furthest down is the lowest. Keeko thinks the Toy Store is lowest because one is the smallest digit, and floor minus three lying further down breaks that doubt.
teaching_notes: One idea: the lowest floor is the one furthest below the ground. Watch for students who pick the smallest digit instead of the floor furthest down.

source: Who is on the lowest floor? 1. Jay is in the Art Centre. So,
video_script.why: A child learns that the lowest floor is the one furthest down, and reads the floor of each shop from the picture.
video_script.substitution: the book's own four friends and their shops, read from the picture
video_script.anchor: four friends in the shops of {{NAME_10}}: the Art Centre, the Sports Centre, the Cinema Centre and the Toy Store
video_script.wrong_answer: the lowest floor is the Toy Store
video_script.wrong_move: picks the floor with the smallest digit, and ignores that floor minus three lies further down
video_script.payoff_line: The lowest floor is the one furthest below the ground.

final_answer.spoken: {{NAME_6}} in the Cinema Centre, on floor minus three

names.{{NAME_10}}: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

hold_back: Answer: {{NAME_6}} (Floor −3) is on the lowest floor.
never_show: the lowest friend before the floors are put on the line
maths_rules: Art Centre is Floor +2; Sports Centre is Floor +5; Cinema Centre is Floor −3; Toy Store is Floor −1.
The lowest floor is the one furthest below the ground: −3.
video_script.design: One idea: the lowest floor is furthest down. One picture throughout; the four floors go on one vertical line. Keeko's doubt is broken by floor minus three lying below floor minus one.
open_questions: The floors of the Sports Centre (+5) and the Cinema Centre (-3) come from the picture and the worklist notes, not from the book text.

<bookmark mark='low'/>The lowest floor is the one that lies furthest down.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says the Toy Store is lowest; on the line, floor −1 sits just under the ground and floor −3 lies two floors further down; the bubble is struck through

marks.look: floor minus one and floor minus three are lit on the line

beats.colours: warning colour for the struck bubble
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the lowest floor is the Toy Store, because one is the smallest digit.
<bookmark mark='look'/>But floor minus one lies right under the ground, and floor minus three lies two floors further down.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Below the ground, a bigger digit means a lower floor, so every floor must be checked.
